_comment: Unit Roadmap spec. Unit title, phase and section titles come from courses/chemistry/DECISIONS.md; do not add them here. 'measured' must agree with DECISIONS.md 'Assessment shape'. Standards follow reports/chem-ohio-standards-verification.md §5 (CONFIRMED rows as main; inference-only, conditional and VIP-for-a-NONE-section rows as support only); key wording from §4.
big_idea: Gas particles are far apart and always moving, and that one model explains how gases behave. Students relate **pressure, volume, temperature** and amount, and use the gas laws to predict what a gas does when one of them changes.

12.1.focus: The particle model of a gas
ican: I can **state** the main assumptions of kinetic molecular theory.
I can **use** the theory to explain pressure and temperature.
I can **convert** between pressure units: atm, mmHg, and kPa.
I can **convert** °C to K and **explain** why gas laws need K.
I can **use** Boyle's, Charles's, and Gay-Lussac's laws.
I can **identify** direct and inverse relationships from data.
I can **use** the combined gas law when pressure, volume, and temperature all change.
I can **derive** each simple gas law from the combined law.
I can **use** Avogadro's law to relate gas volume to moles.
I can **use** 22.4 L/mol at STP to convert liters and moles.
I can **solve** PV = nRT for any variable, choosing the right R.
I can **explain** when real gases stop acting ideal.

standards_source: Ohio's Learning Standards for Science (adopted 2018) · Chemistry
standards_key: pressure, volume and temperature; ideal gas law.
